clauses.clause: Engage in spoken or written dialogue as an author and audience.
clauses.note: Students participate in a Science Talk, take turns, listen, and build onto others’ ideas using sentence frames.

clauses.clause: Make intentional connections within texts.
clauses.note: No explicit student task to connect ideas within a single text is described.

clauses.clause: Make intentional connections between texts.
clauses.note: Students are not directed to compare or connect two texts or sources.

clauses.clause: Make intentional connections beyond texts to other knowledge or experiences.
clauses.note: Students discuss what people are doing when the sun looks a certain way, connecting an image to real-life experiences.

verdicts.evidence: Invite students to take out their Patterns of the Moon notes sheets. Remind them that they will use these notes and take turns responding to their group members' ideas. Direct students' attention to the learning targets and read the first one aloud: 'I can build onto others' ideas while participating in a Science Talk about patterns of the moon.' Remind students that in order to work toward this target, they should try using a sentence frame as they respond to their classmates. Review the previously taught sentence frames: 'I think he/she means __________.' 'I'd like to add ________.' 'This makes me think __________ because ___________.'
verdicts.rationale: Students clearly engage in spoken dialogue as speakers and listeners and make connections to real-life contexts, but there is no explicit activity requiring connections within a single text or between multiple texts.
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Engage in written or spoken dialogue as author and audience for a variety of tasks and purposes, making intentional connections within, between, and beyond texts.

clauses.clause: Discuss texts with others in the group

clauses.clause: Share individual writing with the group
clauses.note: Students write personal notes and in Sky notebooks, but do not share their writing with the group.

clauses.clause: Listen to others as they share their writing
clauses.note: Listening occurs in a Science Talk, not to peers sharing written work.

clauses.clause: Offer feedback on peers' writing
clauses.note: No peer feedback on writing is included.

clauses.clause: Respond to feedback received on own writing
clauses.note: No opportunities to receive or respond to feedback on writing are described.

verdicts.rationale: The lesson centers on a Science Talk about moon patterns and independent note-taking, not on sharing writing or giving/receiving feedback. Norms are reviewed, not developed, and there is no explicit discussion of texts as such.
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Participate in a community of readers and writers by developing group norms, discussing texts, sharing individual writing, listening as others share their writing, and offering and responding to feedback. (I/C)

verdicts.evidence:
- Distribute pencils and the prepared clipboards with Patterns of the Moon notes sheets.
- Focus students on the prompt. Reread it aloud and invite them to begin writing their individual notes.
- Circulate and support students as they write. Remind them to use the Patterns of the Moon anchor chart and Sun, Moon, and Stars Word Wall to help them while writing. If students are having a difficult time explaining their ideas, invite them to look again at Does the Sun Sleep?: Noticing Sun, Moon, and Stars Patterns and jot down what they see or hear that they want to record.
verdicts.rationale: Students research a shared question by gathering information from provided sources and organizing it on a notes sheet, then use it in collaborative discussion.

Remind them to use the Patterns of the Moon anchor chart and Sun, Moon, and Stars Word Wall to help them while writing. If students are having a difficult time explaining their ideas, invite them to look again at Does the Sun Sleep?: Noticing Sun, Moon, and Stars Patterns and jot down what they see or hear that they want to record.
